question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y={2}^{u},\,u=1-x.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}u}={2}^{u}\ln(2),\,\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=-1.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} & =\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}u}\cdot \frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x} \\ & ={2}^{u}\ln(2)\cdot (-1) \\ & =(-1)\cdot {2}^{u}\ln(2) \\ & =-1\cdot {2}^{1-x}\ln(2).\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y = 3\cdot 2^u, \qquad u=1-x.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d u} = 3\cdot 2^u\ln(2),\qquad \dfrac{\textrm d u}{\textrm d x} =-1.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =3\cdot {2}^{u}\ln(2)\cdot (-1) \\  & =-3\cdot {2}^{u}\ln(2) \\  & =-3\cdot {2}^{1-x}\ln(2).\end{aligned}
$$

First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y={3}^{u},\,u=x+{x}^{3}.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}u}={3}^{u}\ln(3),\,\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=1+3{x}^{2}.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} & =\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}u}\cdot \frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x} \\ & ={3}^{u}\ln(3)\cdot (1+3{x}^{2}) \\ & =(1+3{x}^{2})\cdot {3}^{u}\ln(3) \\ & =(1+3{x}^{2})\cdot {3}^{x+{x}^{3}}\ln(3).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at $x=-1$, we have to evaluate $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$ at that point as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m=\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}\big|_{x=-1} & =(1+3(-1)^{2})\cdot {3}^{(-1)+(-1)^{3}}\ln(3) \\ & =4\cdot {3}^{-2}\ln(3) \\ & =\frac{4 \ln{\left(3 \right)}}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $x=-1$ is $\frac{4 \ln{\left(3 \right)}}{9}.$

knowledge_point.title: Differentiating a General Exponential Function Using the Chain Rule

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y=4\cdot {4}^{u},\,u=2+4x.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}u}=4\cdot {4}^{u}\ln(4),\,\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=4.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} & =\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}u}\cdot \frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x} \\ & =4\cdot {4}^{u}\ln(4)\cdot (4) \\ & =(4)\cdot 4\cdot {4}^{u}\ln(4) \\ & =16\cdot {4}^{2+4x}\ln(4).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at $x=-1$, we have to evaluate $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$ at that point as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m=\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}\big|_{x=-1} & =(16)\cdot {4}^{2+4(-1)}\ln(4) \\ & =16\cdot {4}^{-2}\ln(4) \\ & =\ln{\left(4 \right)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $x=-1$ is $\ln{\left(4 \right)}.$

question.:question/problem: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $y={6}^{7x-5}$ at the point where $x=1.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y={6}^{u},\,u=7x-5.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}u}={6}^{u}\ln(6),\,\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=7.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} & =\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}u}\cdot \frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x} \\ & ={6}^{u}\ln(6)\cdot (7) \\ & =(7)\cdot {6}^{u}\ln(6) \\ & =7\cdot {6}^{7x-5}\ln(6).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at $x=1$, we have to evaluate $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$ at that point as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m=\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}\big|_{x=1} & =(7)\cdot {6}^{7(1)-5}\ln(6) \\ & =7\cdot {6}^{2}\ln(6) \\ & =252 \ln{\left(6 \right)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $x=1$ is $252 \ln{\left(6 \right)}.$

Also, the $y$-value of the point on the curve where $x=1$ is

$$
y_1={6}^{2}=36.
$$

Finally, we find the equation of the tangent at that point:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-y_1&=m(x-x_1) \\ y-(36)&=(252 \ln{\left(6 \right)})\left(x-(1)\right) \\ y&=252 x \ln{\left(6 \right)} - 252 \ln{\left(6 \right)} + 36.\end{aligned}
$$
